title: Roslyn Source Generators
description: Generate C# source code at compile time using Roslyn source generators.

data.text: Roslyn Source Generators run during compilation and can add new C# files to your project. They are used by libraries like `System.Text.Json` source generation and `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`.
Source generators are typically distributed as analyzer packages. For development, you reference the generator package in your project.

data.title: Example: Source Generator Package
data.code:
dotnet add package Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp
# Generators are packaged as analyzers (.dll + .pdb)

data.text: A source generator implements `ISourceGenerator` or `IIncrementalGenerator`. The compiler calls it during build, and it can emit additional source files.

data.title: Simple Incremental Generator
Use Generated Code

terms.definition: An older interface for source generators that run once per compilation.
A newer, more efficient interface that runs incrementally on changed inputs.
Adds a generated source file to the compilation.

data.title: Important
data.text: Source generators cannot read or modify existing code, only add new files.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Source generators add code at compile time, not runtime.
Common uses: serialization, logging, mapping, and boilerplate elimination.
data.takeaway: Roslyn source generators reduce runtime cost by generating code at build time.

data.title: Exercise: Create a Source Generator
data.description: Write a source generator that emits a static class with a `Greet` method.
steps: Emit a class with a `SayHello` method.
Reference the generator in a consumer project.
Call the generated method from Main.
data.expectedOutcome: You understand the full lifecycle of a source generator.
